info.name: notification-svc
info.description:
Manual verification for notification-svc (:8133).

=== READ THIS BEFORE RUNNING ANYTHING ===

The canonical Service Input Contract (ZS-ARCH-SVC-001 v2.0 §4) is ENFORCED here in write-strict mode. Every request needs X-Tenant-Id, X-Principal-Id, X-Request-Id and X-Source-Channel; every write additionally needs Idempotency-Key AND X-Legal-Entity-Id. A request missing one is refused with 400 envelope_incomplete BEFORE any handler runs.

That is why this collection mints those headers in a COLLECTION-LEVEL pre-request script rather than listing them per request. Collections on this estate that spelled the headers out per request were all written before enforcement, and every write in them now fails — for a reason that reads like an authorization problem and is not. A script cannot be left off one request the way a header list can.

The script also mints a fresh correlation_id per run, so re-running the collection does not replay the previous run's idempotent sends and report 200s that look like failures.

=== WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE ===

A FAILED delivery comes back 201, deliberately: 03-microservices.md §9.7 requires that notification failure must not collapse the source workflow. Read `status` in the body, never the HTTP code, to learn whether a notice went out.

=== THE HEADER PEOPLE MISS ===

X-Legal-Entity-Id is mandatory on WRITES, separately from the body's legal_entity_id. This service sets LegalEntityID: RequiredOnWrite because a notification is an entity-scoped record (INV-02), so a send or a mark-read without the header is 400 envelope_incomplete before any handler runs. The script below sends it on every request.

=== PREREQUISITES ===

- notification-svc, postgres, authorization-svc and mailpit up (deployments/docker-compose.yml).
- The acting principal holds NOTIFICATION_SEND and NOTIFICATION_VIEW on {{legal_entity_id}} in authorization-svc, or every write answers 403. RUNBOOK.md §'Seeding a grant' has the SQL.
- Mail lands in mailpit at http://localhost:8025 — nothing leaves the machine.

Captured from the first send, used by the read/mark-read requests.

// listed headers by hand now has at least one request missing one —
// which fails with 400 envelope_incomplete and reads like an auth

// record, INV-02), so a send or a mark-read without it is 400

// Mandatory for material state changes only (§4, INV-08). Sending it

request.description: 200 whenever the process is up. Says nothing about the database.
Pings the database pool. This is what the container healthcheck uses: liveness answers 200 with a dead pool, so a service returning 500 on every read would read as healthy.

Look for notification_outbox_pending and notification_outbox_oldest_age_seconds. A pending count that is not falling means the relay is not reaching Kafka, and every governed notice concluded since then has been recorded with no consumer told.

The six compiled-in templates and the variables each refuses to render without. No authorization check and no tenant SCOPE — the catalogue is compiled into the binary, is identical for every tenant and holds no tenant data. It does require a caller identity, checked in the handler: the route previously relied on the envelope middleware for that and the middleware admits reads in write-strict mode, so a bare curl with no headers returned the whole catalogue.

exec: // Strip what the collection script just added, to prove the
// service fails CLOSED rather than serving an unattributed

item.name: 1. POST — IN_APP, free text (201, status SENT)

exec: // IN_APP is the one channel that can honestly claim receipt:
// the register row IS the delivery.

body.raw:
{
  "recipient_principal_id": "{{recipient_principal_id}}",
  "legal_entity_id": "{{legal_entity_id}}",
  "channel": "IN_APP",
  "subject": "Payroll cutoff approaching",
  "body": "Cutoff for the next payroll run is Friday.",
  "source_event_type": "PAYROLL_RUN",
  "source_reference": "pr-2026-09",
  "correlation_id": "pm-{{run_id}}-inapp"
}

request.description: IN_APP is delivered by being recorded. It carries read state, and it is the only channel on which SENT means the recipient can actually see it.

item.name: 2. POST — same correlation_id (200 replay, NOT a second notice)

body.raw:
{
  "recipient_principal_id": "{{recipient_principal_id}}",
  "legal_entity_id": "{{legal_entity_id}}",
  "channel": "IN_APP",
  "subject": "Payroll cutoff approaching",
  "body": "Cutoff for the next payroll run is Friday.",
  "correlation_id": "pm-{{run_id}}-inapp"
}

request.description: Idempotent on (tenant_id, correlation_id). A retried send resolves to the ORIGINAL notification rather than delivering a second copy. Note the body differs from request 1 in nothing that matters — the correlation id is what decides.

item.name: 3. POST — EMAIL with a caller-supplied address (201, provenance REQUEST)

exec: // The override is recorded as such. An address the identity
// authority vouched for and one handed over in the request
// must stay distinguishable after the fact (§0.4).
// SENT here means a provider ACCEPTED it. Not that it arrived.

body.raw:
{
  "recipient_principal_id": "{{recipient_principal_id}}",
  "legal_entity_id": "{{legal_entity_id}}",
  "channel": "EMAIL",
  "subject": "Invoice approval required",
  "body": "Invoice INV-100 needs your approval.",
  "recipient_address": "someone@example.com",
  "correlation_id": "pm-{{run_id}}-email"
}

request.description: Check mailpit at http://localhost:8025 — the message is there, and nothing left the machine. The override exists for recipients who are not established principals yet; normally leave recipient_address out and let identity-context-svc answer.
The template supplies its own subject and body. Values are escaped by the service for the context each lands in, so an organization name containing markup arrives as text.
Mutually exclusive. Accepting both would leave it ambiguous which one the recipient actually received.

item.name: 6. POST — template missing a variable (400 missing_template_variables)

request.description: Refusing beats sending a message with a blank organization name or an empty login link.

item.name: 7. POST — SMS (400 unsupported_channel, NOT a stored FAILED row)

request.description: SMS was accepted, resolved a recipient, and then failed every send — a channel advertising a capability the platform does not have. It is now refused at the boundary like any unrecognised channel. Nothing is recorded: a caller's typo used to leave a permanent FAILED row and a notification.failed event describing an attempt no provider ever saw.

exec: pm.test('refused by the envelope, before any handler', () =>

request.description: This is the request that every pre-enforcement collection on the estate accidentally makes on EVERY write. It is refused before a handler runs, so nothing is recorded.
Authorized against the entity (NOTIFICATION_VIEW), not merely filtered by tenant. Newest first.

Omitting legal_entity_id is a DIFFERENT read: the recipient filter is forced to the calling principal. Authorization used to be conditional on the filter being present, so omitting it — the easier request — returned every notification in the tenant to a principal holding no grant at all.
Refused rather than silently rewritten to the caller. Reading someone else's notices requires legal_entity_id and a grant on it.
Implies IN_APP. read_at is NULL for every email and always will be, so an unfiltered unread read would report every email ever sent as unread.
Authorized against the notification's OWN legal entity, read from the record rather than from the request.
Row-level security hides another tenant's notification. Telling a caller that an id exists elsewhere is itself a disclosure, so the answer is the same one an unknown id gets.
An id that cannot be a UUID names no notification, which is what not found means. The driver's cast failure used to surface as 503 store_unavailable — an outage status for a typo in a URL.
The number on the bell. There is no principal parameter, deliberately: a per-principal unread total anyone could query would report on colleagues' attention.
Only the RECIPIENT may do this. A NOTIFICATION_VIEW grant lets an administrator read the register, and reading the register is not the recipient reading their notice — it must not clear their badge.
Idempotent, and it keeps the first read. Inboxes re-issue this on every render; without the COALESCE, 'when did they first see this' would decay into 'when did they last look'.

Run this against an EMAIL notification's id. This service cannot observe whether a message delivered by an external provider was opened, and does not pretend to. (If {{notification_id}} is the IN_APP one, this returns 200 instead — set it to the EMAIL send's id first.)
